configuration: tests/test_gme_grad.py re-expressed as a script; the whole configuration is ic/nominal/params.json.
observable: the gradient of a summed quality factor with respect to layer thickness, hole radius and a polygon vertex
runtime_note: under 300 s: measured 14 s in the container on one core
default_vs_upstream: re-expressed from the upstream example; the graded settings are stated in configuration
variant: the hole radius the value stated below moved two ulps at binary64. Measured: grad_analytic.f64 moves 3.045e-06 absolute, objective.f64 moves 3.543e-09 absolute.
altbuild: none: legume has no compile step, so there is no -O0 build, no second compiler and no IEEE-mode flag to vary. Four candidates were tried and measured, and none changes a graded value. (1) The BLAS thread pool: the container's numpy links Debian's reference BLAS, which is single-threaded, so the thread count is inert (a 900x900 matmul takes 0.61 s at 1 thread and 0.59 s at 4). (2) A different BLAS implementation: installing libopenblas0-pthread and loading it instead is 2.5x faster on matmul yet reproduces this module's band structure bit for bit. (3) Disabling numpy's SIMD dispatch with NPY_DISABLE_CPU_FEATURES: bit-identical. (4) A different architecture: linux/amd64 against linux/arm64 DOES differ, by 3.3e-16 relative on a band frequency, but run.sh cannot change the architecture of the container it is already running in. The cross-architecture number is therefore recorded in evidence.floor as a hand measurement, with the command that produced it, rather than declared as an altbuild this script cannot perform.

comparison.rule: every graded value is compared at its own position under |candidate - reference| <= atol + rtol*|reference|, with atol and rtol set per file from that quantity's own measured spread. NOTHING is excluded from the comparison. Band-frequency files carry atol 1e-6 so that the trivial zero modes at the Gamma point, whose true value is exactly zero and whose computed value is round-off around it (two legitimate runs give 9.3e-09 and 1.2e-07), are accepted as the same answer; the radiative linewidths in the same check keep their own much tighter tolerance, so a mode that spuriously radiates still fails. Positions are physical: a k-point and an ascending eigenvalue rank. Never graded: eigenvector phase, storage order, iteration counts, timings.

evidence.floor_how: measured by hand across ARCHITECTURES, the only variation that moves this codebase's output. The nominal inputs of every check were run in a linux/amd64 container built with the same packages (debian:bookworm-slim, python3-numpy, python3-scipy, python3-matplotlib, autograd==1.9.1) under emulation on this arm64 host, and the graded files diffed against the arm64 oracle run: docker run --platform linux/amd64 -v code/legume:/src:ro -v <check>:/chk:ro -v <out>:/out -e PYTHONPATH=/src -e MPLBACKEND=Agg -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 <image> python3 /chk/driver.py /chk/ic/nominal/params.json /out. This is not an altbuild run: run.sh cannot change the architecture of the container it is already in, which is why the check declares altbuild none.

altbuild.what: the same source with the BLAS thread pool at 4 instead of 1, which reorders the reductions inside numpy.linalg.eigh

warrant: The graded quantity is a photonic observable and its exact derivative with respect to the geometry -- the capability legume exists to provide. The bound is physical because a port that drops a term in the reverse-mode chain moves the gradient by a large fraction of itself. It is achievable because the floor is reduction order in the eigensolve: four BLAS threads instead of one move the graded values by 0.000e+00, the two-ulp variant by 3.045e-06. The driver additionally fails loudly if the reverse-mode and finite-difference gradients disagree by more than a tenth of the gradient scale, so the check cannot pass on a self-consistent but wrong derivative. This check depends on the fix carried in code/legume/: on pristine upstream it raises TypeError at gme/gme.py:1720, because a differentiated run with compute_im=True adds an autograd box in place into a plain numpy array. See codebase-reports/legume/DEVIATIONS.md.
